title: Pythagorean and tempered scales
description: By default, Xenpaper 3 associates degree 0 and middle C with 12edo middle C below A4 = 440 Hz (about 261.626 Hz). Diatonic intervals themselves follow a pure 3/2 chain of fifths until a temperament is selected.

props.source:
# Ascending Pythagorean Major scale
C= D E F G A B c=
# Descending Pythagorean Major
243/128 27/16 3/2 4/3 81/64 9/8 1/1=
..
# Ascending 12-TET Major
0= 2 4 5 7 9 11 12==
.

title: Nominals and octaves
description: Lower-case nominals are always an octave above upper-case nominals. Primes and graves always refer to octaves.

props.source:
# Minor pentatonic
`A `B D E G A B d e g a b 'd 'e 'g 'a=

title: Staff clefs
description: The upcoming notation view supports treble and bass clef changes. Clef directives affect notation only, not pitch or playback.

props.source:
@clef(treble) C D E F
@clef(bass) `C `D `E `F

title: Relative intervals
description: Relative pitch offsets are supported too.

props.source:
@3
C  P1 1/1       # Perfect unison
C# A1 2187/2048 # Augmented unison
Db m2 256/243   # Minor second
D  M2 9/8       # Major second
Eb m3 32/27     # Minor third
E  M3 81/64     # Major third
F  P4 4/3       # Perfect fourth
Gb d5 1024/729  # Diminished fifth
G  P5 3/2       # Perfect fifth
Ab m6 128/81    # Minor sixth
A  M6 27/16     # Major sixth
Bb m7 16/9      # Minor seventh
B  M7 243/128   # Major seventh
c  P8 2/1       # Perfect octave

title: Pure sharps and flats
description: Note how C# and Db are not the same pitch when tuned pure.

title: Root association
description: You can change which nominal aligns with the root frequency.

title: Tempering diatonic pitches
description: Tuning using an equal temperament like {31edo} automatically affects diatonic notation: C stays with the root, P5 becomes whatever is the closest approximation to 3/2 and the circle of fifths continues from there defining G, D, A, E etc. with increasing drift from Pythagorean intonation.

title: Reversed accidentals
description: If the fifth is tuned very flat the process unfortunately swaps the directions of sharp and flat.

props.source:
{23edo}
# Anti-minor sounds majorish
[`A, C,  E]==.
# Anti-major has a narrow third
[`A, C#, E]==.

title: Ups and downs
description: It is recommended to use Ups and Downs i.e. the caret ^ and v when sharps and flats can be confusing.

props.source:
{16edo}
# Anti-minor
[C, E,  G]==.
# Anti-major using a sensible inflection
[C, vE, G]==.

title: Tempering ratios and chords
description: Use tilde ~ to temper ratios and enumerated chords.

props.source:
{53edo} @pp
# Overtones are locked together
5::15===
.
# Tempered shimmering
~5::15===
.

@mf
# Tempered chord
~[4/3, 7/3, 9/3, 11/3]==
.

# Tempered ratios
~1/1 ~13/10 ~3/2

title: Key signatures
html: Key signatures can be set with {key = G} or modal names like {key = D Dorian}. Plain nominals receive the signature accidentals, while an explicit natural sign ♮ or underscore _ restores the unaltered nominal.

props.source:
# G major sharpens F
{key = G}
G= A B c d e f g=
# Flat seventh to tonic
f_= g=

title: Custom key signatures
description: Custom key signatures allow you to attach ups, lifts, accidentals and inflections to plain nominals. Inflections will be described in detail later. A natural sign restores the original nominal.

title: Pythagorean accidentals
description: Use the pythagorean accidentals p/q (a.k.a. po and qu from Color notation) to jump between named pitches.

title: FJS inflections
html: The Functional Just System lets you spell just intonation by tweaking the Pythagorean spine with small inflections. For example, the Pythagorean major third 81/64 becomes 5/4 by dividing by the syntonic comma 81/80. In FJS, ^5 indicates that prime 5 occurs in the target interval’s numerator; the symbol describes the prime spelling, not necessarily the direction of the pitch adjustment.

title: HEJI inflections
html: HEJI instead chooses the arrow by the inflection’s pitch direction and appends the flavor h to the prime. Consequently, the same 5-limit pitches use the opposite arrow from their FJS spellings.

title: Inflection flavors
description: There's a plethora of different inflection commas used for different purposes. Xenpaper inherits from SonicWeave but syntax-wise only ^ and v are allowed. E.g. 48/35 has to be spelled P4v5v7.

props.source:
{8::16}
0  1  2     3      4  5      6     7     8 ..
# FJS
C D E^5  F^11   G  Ab^13   Bb^7   B^5    c ..
# HEJI
C D Ev5h F^11h  G  Av13h   Bbv7h  Bv5h   c ..
# Neutral FJS
C D Ed^5n F‡^11n G  Ad^13n Bd^7n  Bd^5n  c ..

title: Tempering inflections
description: Inflections respond to tempering.

props.source:
# Harmonic seventh in JI
[G B^5 d f^7]== .

# Harmonic seventh in 19-TET
{19edo}
[G B^5 d f^7]== .
# i.e.
[11 17 22 26]== .

title: Half-intervals
html: Every even equal temperament of the octave contains the semioctave √2 (i.e. 1\2 or 600c) while every odd edo (besides 1edo) has a good approximation to either the neutral third √3/√2 or the semifourth 2/√3.

title: Neutral chords
description: Neutral chords fall exactly between minor and major.

props.source:
[1/1, 32/27,     3/2]==.  # Pythagorean minor
[1/1, 6/5,       3/2]==.  # 5-limit minor
[1/1, 11/9,      3/2]==.  # 11-limit neutral
[1/1, sqrt(3/2), 3/2]==.  # true neutral
[1/1, 5/4,       3/2]==.  # 5-limit major
[1/1, 81/64,     3/2]==.  # Pythagorean major

title: Semiquartal chords
description: Semiquartal chords can be fun to mess around with.

title: Semioctave chords
html:
Note that fractions in Xenpaper 3 are "vertical" and bind more strongly than exponentiation. (PEMDAS-like division is available as div).

The semi-octave is familiar from 12edo but can be used in other contexts as well.

props.source:
4:5:6:7==.                      # harmonic 7th
[1/1, 5/4, 3/2, sqrt(25/8)]==.  # true √2 against the third

title: Half-accidentals in 10edo
html: When the closest approximation to 3/2 spans an even number of edosteps it often makes sense to use half-sharps (𝄲, ‡ or t) and half-flats (𝄳 or d) to reach the neutral third n3.

title: Quartertone key signatures
description: Key signatures support quartertones.

title: Relative neutral intervals
description: Relative neutral intervals fall exactly between minor and major, mid fourth falls between perfect and augmented, while mid fifth falls between diminished and perfect. Like other relative intervals, they follow the active temperament.

props.source:
Ct  SA1   # Semi-augmented unison
Ddb sd2   # Semi-diminished second
Dd  n2    # Neutral second
Dt  SA2   # Semi-augmented second
Ed  n3    # Neutral third
Fd  sd4   # Semi-diminished fourth
Ft SA4 n4 # Semi-augmented i.e. mid fourth
Gd sd5 n5 # Semi-diminished i.e. mid fifth
Gt  SA5   # Semi-augmented fifth

title: Interordinal nominals
description: 12edo hides scales that repeat twice every octave.

props.source:
{12edo}
C D E F Gam Del Eps Zet c
..
C Eta D Alp E F Gam G Del A Eps Zet c

title: Greek nominals in 22edo
description:
Unfortunately a semioctave above C falls exactly between F and G so we need a new nominal Gam (Gamma) for this purpose. (The fifthwards tritone F# may be tuned unpredictably and rarely matches the fourthwards tritone Gb.) Every interordinal nominal is related to a Latin nominal by a semioctave. Alp is a 1\2 below A, Bet is a 1\2 below B, Gam is a 1\2 above C, etc. to stay within the C to c range.

The scales retain much of their character in 22edo. Highlight colors help to differentiate Greek script from Latin. On the staff Greek notes obtain a triangle note-head.

props.source:
{22edo}
C D E F Γ Δ Ε Ζ c
..
C Η D Α E F Γ G Δ A Ε Ζ c

title: Semioctave key signatures
description: Key signatures translate across semioctaves.

props.source:
{key = F major}
F Zet G eta A alp
# Both B and Bet become flat
B bet

c gam d del e eps f Zet F=

title: Relative semioctave intervals
html: Relative semi-octave intervals exist and are interordinal. E.g. P8 / 2 is P4½. The ASCII for "½" is "h" in this context.

props.source:
Eta P1½
Alp M2½
Bet M3½
Gam P4h
Del M5h
Eps M6½
Zet P7½

title: Semiquartal scales in 19edo
description: When the closest approximation to 4/3 spans an even number of edosteps you may combine half-accidentals with interordinals to reach the semifourth.

props.source:
{19edo}
C D Alpd Betd F G Deld Epsd Bb c

title: Relative semiquartal intervals
description: Relative semiquartal intervals are spelled as neutral qualities of interordinals.

props.source:
n2½ P4 / 2
n3½ M6 / 2
n5½ m10 / 2
n6½ P8 - P4 / 2

title: Custom ups and downs
description: The Ups-and-Downs inflection is customizable.

props.source:
# Make ups septimal
{^ = 64/63}
# Down-minor is 6:7:9
[`A vC E]== .
# Up-major is 14:18:21
[`A ^C# E]== .

title: Custom lifts and drops
description: By default a tempered lift is worth 5 ups, but can be configured separately.

title: Inflected scale degrees
description: Ups and lifts attach to numeric scale degrees too.

title: Recovering just intonation
description: Automatic tempering can be undone by setting the scale to {Pythagorean} or {JI}.

title: Syntonic accidentals
description: 5-limit intervals are available using syntonic accidentals 𝄬, 𝄭, 𝄮, 𝄯, 𝄰 and 𝄱 which adjust pitch by 81/80.

title: Jubilismic lifts
description: 7-limit intervals use the jubilismic √(50/49) lift slash / and the drop backslash \ to turn interordinals back into just intonation.

props.source:
# 5:6:7 on C
[C E𝄬 \Gam]==

title: Rastmic ups and downs
description: 11-limit intervals go through neutrals using the rastmic √(243/242) up caret ^ and the down v.

title: Wart notation
description: Instead of "edo" you can use Wart Notation to select a different prime mapping.

props.source:
{A = 440Hz}
# This progression would drift with plain
# {17edo} so we use the 17c val instead.
{17c}
|:@x10
[`A Cv5 E]
[Cv5 E Gv5]
[`B Dv5 Gv5]
[`Av5 Dv5 F#]
{root = Av5} :|

title: Custom prime mappings
description: Custom prime mappings are supported.
